plain_text:
Breast cancer is the second most common type
of cancer in women in the United States, and
a mammogram, which is an x-ray of the breast,
semantic_text: Breast cancer is the second most common type of cancer in women in the United States, and a mammogram, which is an x-ray of the breast,

plain_text:
is one of the best ways to detect it. Getting mammograms at
recommended times, even if you don't have symptoms, is key to
finding breast cancer early.
semantic_text: is one of the best ways to detect it. Getting mammograms at recommended times, even if you don't have symptoms, is key to finding breast cancer early.

plain_text:
Detecting it early means more effective treatment options
and better outcomes. Women between ages 50 and 69 who get
mammograms have a lower chance of dying from breast cancer
than women who do not get them.
semantic_text: Detecting it early means more effective treatment options and better outcomes. Women between ages 50 and 69 who get mammograms have a lower chance of dying from breast cancer than women who do not get them.

plain_text:
Fewer than 10% of women called back
for more tests after a mammogram are
found to have breast cancer.
semantic_text: Fewer than 10% of women called back for more tests after a mammogram are found to have breast cancer.

plain_text:
"Abnormal" is how doctors describe a mammogram
that shows something has changed in your breast.
To find out what's causing the changes, your provider

plain_text:
may recommend diagnostic tests. These would be additional
imaging tests such as an ultrasound or a magnetic resonance
imaging (MRI) scan.

plain_text:
Your doctor may order a breast biopsy as well. A biopsy is a
procedure where a small sample of cells, fluids, or tissue is taken and
examined under a microscope. The test happens in a doctor's office,
clinic, or hospital (but you can go home the same day).

plain_text:
